newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Floods cause havoc in Manila, close markets.
newsitem.headline: Floods cause havoc in Manila, close markets.

text.p: Three days of torrential rains and heavy seas have caused havoc in the Philippines, killing at least six people and shutting down Manila streets and financial markets on Monday.
The six were killed at the weekend when their pleasure boat capsized off the central island of Cebu.
But the worst of the rains and flooding were on the northern Philippine island of Luzon, where the capital Manila ground to a halt and volcanic mudflows closed some provincial roads.
The rains marked the end of a long dry season that had some parts of the country running short of water.
The rainy season usually begins around May and lasts until November, averaging more than 20 typhoons during the period.
Manila's stock market managed to stay open for only 15 minutes before officials closed it for the day. Banks in the capital had all but stopped trading.

Power was cut off in many parts of Manila in the morning. Thousands of workers were stranded as buses and cars were unable to drive through the often waist-high water, forcing several private and government offices to close for the day.

A three-foot (one metre) deep mudflow cascaded down river-beds, bringing down tonnes of volcanic rock and ash left over from the 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo, said National Disaster Coordinating Council executive officer Fortunato Dejoras in a report to the president.
The Weather Bureau warned that the rains, the result of an active low pressure area hovering over Luzon island, would continue until Tuesday.
Six domestic flights out of Manila were cancelled and a number of international flights delayed because of poor visibility.
